content: Ritonavir and atazanavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Ritonavir enhances the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. Ritonavir significantly increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. The recommended dosage of atogepant, an OATP1B1 substrate, when used with OATP inhibitors, is 10 mg or 30 mg once daily. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of atomoxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while atorvastatin increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction can lead to increased toxicity of atorvastatin, including a higher risk of myopathy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse events, including hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of avatrombopag by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. Close monitoring is required. Azithromycin increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, ritonavir also decreases their levels by increasing metabolism. This reduction in bazedoxifene exposure may increase the risk of endometrial hyperplasia. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels of berotralstat via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of betibeglogene autotemcel. Avoid antiretroviral medications for at least one month before mobilization or until all apheresis cycles are completed, as they may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis cells. Ritonavir increases the levels of betrixaban via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, then 40 mg daily if co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. Monitor closely. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of bexagliflozin by inducing UGT1A9 metabolism. Consider adding another antihyperglycemic agent if additional glycemic control is required. Monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bosentan decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Ritonavir also increases bosentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for adverse reactions. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. If also co-administered with a strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. Monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be avoided, reduce the brigatinib dose by 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. Ritonavir increases bromocriptine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine (including buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for signs of overmedication or toxicity. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, consider transitioning to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. Monitor closely for withdrawal symptoms if the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued. Ritonavir decreases bupropion levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Bupropion levels may decrease by 20-80%, and dose adjustments may be required. Monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Butabarbital and butalbital decrease ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases cabazitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration due to the potential for increased toxicity. Monitor closely. Ritonavir increases cabergoline levels by inhibiting metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases cabozantinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If required, reduce the cabozantinib dose and monitor for toxicity. Resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. Ritonavir increases calcifediol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustment of calcifediol may be required, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium levels should be closely monitored when initiating or discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Ritonavir increases calcitriol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Ritonavir decreases canagliflozin levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider alternative antihyperglycemic agents in patients with eGFR <73 mL/min/1.73 m². Ritonavir increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. Ritonavir increases capivasertib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration cannot be avoided, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. Ritonavir increases capmatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor plasma levels closely. Carbamazepine decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases cariprazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors requires cariprazine dose reduction. Refer to the drug monograph for dosage modification. Monitor closely. Ritonavir increases carvedilol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cenobamate decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
